chapter: Gene Mayl, Teddy Buckner and the Dixie Flies
title: Playing in Gene Mayl's band in Dayton
summary: Joe describes the Rhythm Kings' members and the club job that ended the band.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: So anyway, then you went back and played with Gene Mayl's band.
How were they to play with?

It wasn't a very good band, if that's what you mean. I'm trying to think... I can't remember all of the guys. The trumpet player was an old guy who came from New York; he used to have the Red Onion band in New York. Do you know who I'm talking about? Bob. What the devil is his name...? Bob Hodes.

Well, anyway, he was a trumpet player. And he had a banjo player named Jack Bastheim, and naturally Gene was on bass. They had a trombone player that had just been over in England working, who had come back to the band. And we played around Dayton for a long time, and a place where we had been working, a Greek.... And George and I had a restaurant, a club called the Hitching Post. So he wanted to cut down on the band, and Gene, he says, "I would like..." He said, "I'll keep you in the band if you want to stay." So he made me an offer, a good offer. So I told
Gene, "I'm going to stay." He said he was going to fire the whole band. And Gene didn't have nothin' too much anyway at the time, because when this job folded, that was it.
